prs.title: Fix infinite reconnection loop in StreamableHTTP client
prs.author: Dharit13
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client ultimately fails (max retries exhausted / reconnection attempt raises), the failure is currently swallowed silently — the caller is left waiting forever with no error and no exception. Both PRs patch the same failure branch in `_handle_reconnection` to surface that failure, just via different channels: #2395 sends a JSON-RPC error response back through `read_stream_writer` for the specific pending request; #3098 instead makes the failure raise a catchable `StreamableHTTPError` (unwrapped from the anyio ExceptionGroup) out of the client context manager. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: When SSE stream reconnection in the StreamableHTTP client ultimately fails (max retries exhausted / reconnection attempt raises), the failure is currently swallowed silently — the caller is left waiting forever with no error and no exception. Both PRs patch the same failure branch in `_handle_reconnection` to surface that failure, just via different channels: #2395 sends a JSON-RPC error response back through `read_stream_writer` for the specific pending request; #3098 instead makes the failure raise a catchable `StreamableHTTPError` (unwrapped from the anyio ExceptionGroup) out of the client context manager. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2395's change is scoped entirely inside the existing `attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS` branch and preserves current control flow (function still returns normally after emitting the error), and it guards with `isinstance(ctx.session_message.message, JSONRPCRequest)` so it only emits an error when there's actually a pending request awaiting a response — avoiding spurious errors for notifications. #3098's approach instead turns the failure into a raised exception that propagates through the task group (needing a separate `_unwrap_exception` helper to dig it out of the resulting ExceptionGroup), which tears down the whole session/task group rather than just failing the one in-flight call, and its diff also touches an unrelated line (`from __future__ import annotations as _annotations` -> `from __future__ import annotations`), widening the change's surface and merge-conflict risk beyond the reconnection fix itself.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/regex matching instead of proper comma-delimited auth-param tokenization, causing false-positive matches when a param name appears as a substring elsewhere in the header (e.g. inside a quoted value or another param). prs.cluster_pick_reason: PR #3041 explicitly locates the Bearer challenge before extracting its params (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params identifies which comma-separated segment starts with the 'Bearer' scheme token), so it correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). prs.title: Fix pre_parse_json corrupting str | None values that look like JSON
prs.author: vientooscuro
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py incorrectly calls json.loads() on string arguments typed as unions containing str (most commonly `str | None`), corrupting valid string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a plain string payload like '{"a":1}') by silently turning them into parsed dicts/lists instead of leaving them as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: pre_parse_json() in func_metadata.py incorrectly calls json.loads() on string arguments typed as unions containing str (most commonly `str | None`), corrupting valid string values that happen to look like JSON (e.g. a plain string payload like '{"a":1}') by silently turning them into parsed dicts/lists instead of leaving them as strings. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both add a helper to decide when pre_parse_json should skip json.loads(), but #2032's `_should_pre_parse_json` checks union members via `arg not in _SIMPLE_TYPES` (a frozenset of bare `str`/`int`/`float`/`bool`/`NoneType`) without stripping `Annotated[...]` first. members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Stored/reloaded OAuth tokens never get token_expiry_time recomputed on context initialization, so is_token_valid() treats an actually-expired stored access token as valid. #1784 fixes this at the root by calling context.update_token_expiry() in _initialize() when stored tokens are loaded, with a dedicated expired_tokens test fixture. #2875 works around the exact same bug (its own inline comment states 'a provider reloaded from storage never restores token_expiry_time, so is_token_valid() treats the stale token as valid') by adding a new stored-refresh-token-before-full-reauth branch inside the 401 handler of async_auth_flow, instead of correcting the state that is wrong in the first place. clusters.pick_reason: PR #3041 explicitly locates the Bearer challenge before extracting its params (_split_www_authenticate_segments + _extract_bearer_auth_params identifies which comma-separated segment starts with the 'Bearer' scheme token), so it correctly handles headers containing multiple challenges (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer realm="y"'). PR #3012's _iter_www_auth_params only strips text before the first space in the whole header and treats everything after it as one scheme's params, which mis-parses headers with more than one challenge. #3041's approach is the more complete fix for the same underlying tokenization bug.

members.title: fix(auth): match complete WWW-Authenticate parameters
members.author: tarunag10
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3041: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py: WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive substring/regex matching instead of proper comma-delimited auth-param tokenization, causing false-positive matches when a param name appears as a substring elsewhere in the header (e.g. inside a quoted value or another param). Both fixes introduce a manual character-by-character scanner that splits on top-level commas while tracking quoted-string state and backslash escapes, so params are only matched at real token boundaries.
